answer: Agents deposit stake bonds to transact, and peers re-execute all receipts; each Sybil must bond additional resources, incurring a per-identity fee tied to the zephyr’s entropy pool. The tide of re-execution validates receipts in sequence, forcing attackers to litigate each clone linearly along the river’s grade. The cost: each extra identity burns a bonded token and delays consensus by 3ms of serial proof checking, unbounded by parallel farms. This works because arbitrary farmer supply cannot flood the bond market or batch one-way proofs.
